40940-johnny-ludlow-fourth-series.title: Johnny Ludlow
40940-johnny-ludlow-fourth-series.creator: Mrs. Henry Wood
40940-johnny-ludlow-fourth-series.description: A book by Mrs. Henry Wood. prettier girls than Ellin Delorane, but never one that the heart so quickly went out to. She was too much like her dead mother; had the same look of fragile delicacy, the same sweet face with its pensive sadness, the soft brown eyes and the lovely complexion. Delorane had died of decline: people would say to one another, in confidence, they hoped Ellin might escape it.

6855-ideala.title: Ideala
6855-ideala.creator: Unknown
6855-ideala.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. She came among us without flourish of trumpets. She just slipped into her place, almost unnoticed, but once she was settled there it seemed as if we had got something we had wanted all our lives, and we should have missed her as you would miss the thrushes in the spring, or any other sweet familiar thing. But what the secret of her charm was I cannot say. She was full of inconsistencies.

arxiv-2112-04175.title: Embeddings of the symmetric groups to the space Cremona group Thanks: This work is supported by the Russian Science Foundation under grant №18-11-00121.
arxiv-2112-04175.creator: Yuri Prokhorov
arxiv-2112-04175.description: Abstract 1. Introduction The classification of finite subgroups in the Cremona groups \operatorname{Cr}_{n}(\mathbb{C}) is an old-standing problem that goes back to works of classics of Italian algebraic geometry. In the last two decades the interest to this problem was reactivated; see for example [ DI09 ] , [ Pro21b ] , and references therein.

arxiv-2203-10614.title: Does DQN really learn? Exploring adversarial training schemes in Pong
arxiv-2203-10614.creator: Bowen He, Sreehari Rammohan, Jessica Forde, Michael L. Littman
arxiv-2203-10614.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bowen He, Sreehari Rammohan, Jessica Forde, Michael L. Littman. In this work, we study two self-play training schemes, Chainer and Pool , and show they lead to improved agent performance in Atari Pong compared to a standard DQN agent—trained against the built-in Atari opponent.

arxiv-2207-13022.title: Fast Scrambling of Mutual Information in Kerr- A ​ d ​ S 4 AdS_{4}
arxiv-2207-13022.creator: Vinay Malvimat a , Rohan R. Poojary b
arxiv-2207-13022.description: Abstract We compute the disruption of mutual information between the hemispherical subsystems on the left and right CFT s s of a Thermofield Double state described by a Kerr geometry in A ​ d ​ S 4 AdS_{4} due to shockwaves along the equatorial plane. The shockwaves and the subsystems considered respect the axi-symmetry of the geometry.

arxiv-2208-13094.title: Measuring the Prevalence of Anti-Social Behavior in Online Communities DOI: xx.xxxx/xxxxxxx.xxxxxxx Conference: This work will appear in CSCW ’22: Proc. ACM Hum.-Comput. Interact; November 03–05, 2022; Woodstock, NY This work will appear in CSCW ’22: Proc. ACM Hum.-Comput. Interact, June 03–05, 2022
arxiv-2208-13094.creator: Joon Sung Park, Joseph Seering, Michael S. Bernstein
arxiv-2208-13094.description: Abstract . With increasing attention to online anti-social behaviors such as personal attacks and bigotry, it is critical to have an accurate accounting of how widespread anti-social behaviors are. In this paper, we empirically measure the prevalence of anti-social behavior in one of the world’s most popular online community platforms.

arxiv-2303-03185.title: Evaluation of Confidence-based Ensembling in Deep Learning Image Classification
arxiv-2303-03185.creator: Rafael Rosales, Peter Popov, Michael Paulitsch
arxiv-2303-03185.description: Abstract Ensembling is a successful technique to improve the performance of machine learning (ML) models. Conf-Ensemble is an adaptation to Boosting to create ensembles based on model confidence instead of model errors to better classify difficult edge-cases. The key idea is to create successive model experts for samples that were difficult (not necessarily incorrectly classified) by the preceding model.

arxiv-2405-17493.title: Overcoming Negative Transfer by Online Selection: Distant Domain Adaptation for Fault Diagnosis
arxiv-2405-17493.creator: Ziyan Wang, Mohamed Ragab, Wenmian Yang, Min Wu, Sinno Jialin Pan, Jie Zhang, Zhenghua Chen
arxiv-2405-17493.description: Abstract Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has achieved remarkable success in fault diagnosis, bringing significant benefits to diverse industrial applications. While most UDA methods focus on cross-working condition scenarios where the source and target domains are notably similar, real-world applications often grapple with severe domain shifts.

arxiv-2406-14811.title: Non-Markovian Collective Emission of Giant emitters in the Zeno Regime
arxiv-2406-14811.creator: Qing-Yang Qiu, Xin-You Lü
arxiv-2406-14811.description: Abstract We explore the collective Zeno dynamics of giant artificial atoms that are coupled, via multiple coupling points, to a common photonic or acoustic reservoir. In this regime, the establishment of atomic cooperativity and the revivification of exponential decay are highly intertwined, which is utterly beyond the non-Markovian regime with only retarded backaction.

arxiv-2503-20715.title: From Annotation to Adaptation: Metrics, Synthetic Data, and Aspect Extraction for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models
arxiv-2503-20715.creator: Nikita Neveditsin, Pawan Lingras, Vijay Mago
arxiv-2503-20715.description: Abstract This study examines the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA), with a focus on implicit aspect extraction in a novel domain. Using a synthetic sports feedback dataset, we evaluate open-weight LLMs’ ability to extract aspect-polarity pairs and propose a metric to facilitate the evaluation of aspect extraction with generative models.

myers-human-personality-1903.description: Posthumous masterwork founding the theory of the subliminal self — the single most cited text in psychical research.

pmc-11412991.title: Analysis of vibration signals near ground surface during blasting excavation of a tunnel in fractured rock
pmc-11412991.creator: Zuhua Deng, Junyu Meng, Yongfeng Deng, Junjun Ni, Daicheng Ye
pmc-11412991.description: This study aims to analyze the vibration signals near the ground surface due to the underneath drilling and blasting activities in a fissured rock tunnel. Blasting induced vibration on the ground surface was continuously monitored in a fissured rock tunnel drilling and blasting excavation project in field.

pmc-11476593.title: An example of the adaptation of the Nominal Group Technique (NGT) to a virtual format (vNGT) within healthcare research
pmc-11476593.creator: Frances Riley-Bennett, Lal Russell, Rebecca Fisher
pmc-11476593.description: The Nominal Group Technique (NGT) has been used to establish clinical priorities and generate guidelines within healthcare since its creation over fifty years ago. It is characterised by its five distinct stages; introduction, silent idea generation, ‘round robin’, clarifications and rating or ranking.

pmc-11501444.title: Development of Pericarditis Following Implantation of Micra Leadless Pacemaker
pmc-11501444.creator: Anita M Medepalli, Blake T Edwards, Harry Eyituoyo, Pooja Patel, David C Parish
pmc-11501444.description: Pacemakers are frequently essential in managing conduction disorders. Recently, the advancement of leadless pacemakers (LPs) has emerged, offering an alternative without the need for an upper shoulder incision or pacing leads. Despite the advantages, including reduced infection risk and improved durability, the novel nature of LPs means that some complications are still being identified.

pmc-11593748.title: Asymmetric polarization by vaccination status identification during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11593748.creator: Sebastian Jungkunz
pmc-11593748.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). COVID-19 prevention measures and vaccine policies have led to substantial polarization across the world. I investigate whether and how vaccination status and vaccination status identification affect the sympathy and prejudice for vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. Drawing on a preregistered vignette survey experiment in a large representative sample from Germany (n = 6,100) in December 2021, I show that prejudice was greater among the vaccinated towards the unvaccinated than vice versa.

pmc-12611043.title: Salmonellosis Outbreak in a Rottweiler Kennel Associated with Raw Meat-Based Diets
pmc-12611043.creator: Betina Boneva-Marutsova, Plamen Marutsov, Marie-Louise Geisler, Georgi Zhelev, Librado Carrasco
pmc-12611043.description: Simple SummaryThis report outlines an outbreak of salmonellosis in a Rottweiler breeding kennel caused by Salmonella Agona, which was linked to an unlicensed raw meat-based diet. It emphasises the importance of safe feeding practices, good biosecurity measures, and traceable feed sources in kennels. Additionally, it raises awareness about the zoonotic risks associated with raw feeding.

pmc-13008903.title: Biomechanical behavior of endocrowns with different axial wall heights: a finite-element study
pmc-13008903.creator: Waleed M. S. Al Qahtani, Mohammad Zarbah, Nasser Hussein Shaheen, Ali Barakat, Hend Mohamed Elsayed, Shaimaa F. K. Habib, Lama Ahmed Alqahtani, Ebaa Ibrahim Alagha, Salah A. Yousief, Diaaeldin Farag
pmc-13008903.description: IntroductionThe aim of this study was to compare endocrown restorations of mandibular first molars using four distinct preparation designs with different residual tooth heights by employing finite-element analysis. A butt joint marginal design was compared with three shoulder finish line preparations.Materials and methodsFour three-dimensional finite-element models were developed to represent different endocrown configurations.

pmc-13169989.title: Optimizing Resource Utilization in Low- and Middle-Income Country NICUs: A Clinical Audit of Surgical Infection Screening Practices at a High-Volume NICU in Pakistan
pmc-13169989.creator: Humza Thobani, Rafia Durrani, Muhammad Osama Khan, Javeria Javed, Sulaiman Sajjad, Zahra Iftikhar, Muhammad Aqil Soomro, Saqib Qazi, Faraz Ali Khan, Saleem Islam
pmc-13169989.description: Objective:Post operative sepsis in neonates is a serious problem that may be challenging to diagnose. It is standard practice at our Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) in Pakistan to perform routine Blood Cultures (BLCS) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) to screen for post-operative sepsis. We aimed to review this practice to investigate its effectiveness at screening for post-operative sepsis.

pmc-13275170.title: Changes in White Blood Cell and Neutrophil Counts in Patients With Schizophrenia Treated With Lithium Carbonate, Adenine, and Ninjin‐Yoei‐To: A Preliminary Study
pmc-13275170.creator: Teruyuki Matsuoka, Sumihiro Yamano
pmc-13275170.description: AimClozapine is often unavailable to patients with treatment‐resistant schizophrenia when white blood cell (WBC) and neutrophil counts do not meet the required thresholds. This study aimed to examine changes in WBC and neutrophil counts and the factors associated with these changes.MethodsThirty‐five patients with schizophrenia who received adenine, Ninjin‐yoei‐to, or lithium carbonate were included in the treatment group.
